title: Rabbi Simon son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned at the beginning of Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:5. Hyman says it should undoubtedly read “in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.” Hyman takes the written abbreviation (ב״ד in the supplied text) to mean “in the name of Rabbi” and says it came to be read as בר׳, “son of Rabbi.”

notes.text: Hyman proposes replacing a genealogical “son of Rabbi” with a reporting formula “in the name of Rabbi.” The frozen abbreviation ב״ד in his explanation remains unclear and is preserved, not silently emended.

The saved named Guggenheimer Megillah 1:5 paragraph explicitly has Rabbi Simon in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi. It supports Hyman’s reporting-formula comparison without proving the supplied ב״ד abbreviation or its alleged development into בר׳. Hyman’s “undoubtedly” remains his own assertion; no father–son identity is admitted.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 964) has ב״ר in the explanation, where the supplied Hebrew has ב״ד. In the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:5, Rabbi Simon reports in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi in the discussion of reading the Megillah in the second Adar. That reading supports the reporting formula. The proposed history of the abbreviation is Hyman’s.
